title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a survey of 'canonical Riemannian metrics on a conformal surface without boundary'. Conformal surfaces are allowed to be non-orientable, X^or denotes the orientation double cover, and the classification is by the universal cover.

(End of case 1, the hyperbolic case.) The metric of curvature −1 is obtained by descent from the universal cover. A bracketed remark notes the alternative normalization of total area = 1.

(Genus 1 case.) If X^or is an elliptic curve C/Λ, there is a unique flat metric that is compatible with the conformal structure, invariant by translations, and of total area 1. All automorphisms of C/Λ, holomorphic or antiholomorphic, are affine z ↦ uz+b or z ↦ u z̄ + b with |u| = 1. So they preserve this metric. Hence in the non-orientable case (Klein bottle) the canonical metric of X^or descends to X.

(Case 2'.) X ≅ C*, or X = real projective plane minus a point (open Möbius band), i.e. X non-orientable with X^or ≅ C*. As in the previous case, descent from the universal cover C → C*, z ↦ exp(2πiz), gives a flat metric. It is |dz|² on C, i.e. |dw|²/|w|² on C*, canonical up to a positive scalar. The automorphisms of C* are w ↦ aw and w ↦ a/w (a ∈ C*). On C they correspond to z ↦ z+α and z ↦ −z+α, and all of them preserve the metric.

The next page completes the step:
- Normalize so that the circle |w| = 1 has length 1. This gives a flat cylinder of circumference 1, defined uniformly on every X ≅ C*.
- Note that w ↦ w̄ also preserves it, so every conformal or anticonformal automorphism preserves it.
- Descend to the Möbius band.

Purpose: in a manuscript on 'surgery of conformal surfaces', to equip each surface type, especially the cylinder C* that serves as the gluing piece in surgery, with a canonical metric that is invariant under all conformal automorphisms.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor point: the canonical metric on C* is only defined after a normalization choice, which is supplied on the next page (length of |z|=1 equal to 1). On this page it is correctly stated as 'mod multiplication by a scalar >0'.
Numbering is inconsistent: the page has '2')' while the next page has '2°) Cas X ≃ E_C'. This reflects the draft character of the notes.

ideas.what: Canonical flat metric on a genus-1 conformal surface (translation-invariant, area 1), invariant under all conformal and anticonformal automorphisms, hence descending to the Klein bottle
ideas.modern_name: Flat metric from uniformization / Haar measure normalization on complex tori

ideas.what: Canonical flat cylinder metric |dz|²/|z|² on C*, invariant under z↦az, z↦a/z, z↦z̄, descending to the open Möbius band
ideas.modern_name: Flat cylinder metric (as used in Strebel/Jenkins–Strebel differentials and plumbing constructions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; cylinders as gluing pieces in Strebel (1984) and in plumbing/Fenchel–Nielsen-type surgery

ideas.what: Systematic treatment of possibly non-orientable conformal surfaces via the orientation cover X^or, with descent of canonical metrics
ideas.modern_name: Klein surfaces / dianalytic structures; descent along the orientation double cover

deep.surprise_reason: Routine uniformization facts carefully adapted to non-orientable surfaces. The only mild interest is the context: canonical flat cylinders as preparation for Grothendieck's 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes'. That context is documented elsewhere in the cote, not on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'la métrique canonique de X^{an} (qui est une courbe elliptique /C) ne dépend que de X^{an}' should read roughly 'la métrique canonique de X^{or} (qui est une courbe elliptique /C) se descend à X'. This is the non-oriented (Klein bottle) case.
'Il s'ensuit que dans le cas envisagé' is likely 'Il s'ensuit que dans le cas non orienté'.
'[i.e. X non stable [?] et X^{an} ≃ C*]' should be '[i.e. X non orientable et X^{or} ≃ C*]'.
'Le cas X ≃ C*, comme dans 2, des ... discrets [?] à partir des revêtements universels' is likely 'Dans le cas X ≃ C*, comme dans 2, en descendant à partir des revêtements universels'.
'Les automorphismes de C* sont stables de la forme z→az, sont z→a/z' should be 'Les automorphismes de C* sont de la forme z→az, ou z→a/z'.
'Donc en divisant la métrique sur C*' is likely 'Donc en descendant la métrique sur C*'.
